2027-04-20.title: Tuesday after the Third Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: Do not spurn the blood of the covenant
You cannot serve God and wealth; what God has joined
2027-04-20.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Third Sunday after the Resurrection.
2027-04-20.verse: No slave can serve two masters; for a slave will either hate the one and love the other, or be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
theo: Christ is risen! Today's Gospel is plain speech about money. “If then you have not been faithful with the dishonest wealth, who will entrust to you the true riches?” Then the sentence everyone remembers: “No slave can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and wealth.” Jesus does not say that money is evil; he says it makes a poor master. Wealth asks for the whole heart, and so does God; one of them must give way. Luke adds that some who heard this “were lovers of money” and ridiculed him, and Jesus answers: “God knows your hearts; for what is prized by human beings is an abomination in the sight of God.” The warning is for every listener in every age, and the Catechism repeats the bold words of St John Chrysostom: not to let the poor share in our goods is to steal from them and deprive them of life; the goods we possess are not ours, but theirs (Catechism 2446). The risen Lord does not ask us to despise the world; he asks us to use what passes so as to gain what lasts.

Then Jesus speaks of the law: “it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one stroke of a letter in the law to be dropped,” and he gives one example where he restores God's first plan: “Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery.” Jesus takes marriage back to the beginning, when God made man and woman to become “one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). The Church holds that a valid, consummated marriage between baptized persons cannot be dissolved by any human power (Catechism 1614–1615, 2382). This teaching is a word of protection, especially for wives who in the ancient world could be sent away with a single document. It is never a reason to treat with coldness those whose marriages have broken down. Many were abandoned against their will; many carry wounds. The Church is asked to accompany them with patience and love, to help them examine their situation in truth, and to keep them close to the life of the parish (Pope Francis, Amoris Laetitia, 2016).

The Letter to the Hebrews today sounds severe: “if we willfully persist in sin after having received the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,” and “It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.” What does it mean? The Letter has spent chapters showing that Christ's one sacrifice is the only sacrifice for sin. Whoever deliberately rejects it, trampling on “the Son of God” and outraging “the Spirit of grace,” turns away from the only remedy there is. In the third century some, like the followers of Novatian, read these lines as if the Church could never forgive grave sin after Baptism. The Church rejected that reading and kept the door of Penance open: there is no offence, however serious, that the Church cannot forgive (Catechism 982). On the very evening of his Resurrection the Lord breathed on the apostles and gave them power to forgive sins (John 20:22–23). The fearful thing is not the hand of God but refusing it. King David once chose: “let us fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercy is great” (2 Samuel 24:14). Let that be our choice too, in the confessional this Easter.
outline: Ask: who is really the master of my money, my time and my heart?
Money is a useful servant and a poor master.
Marriage restored to the beginning, and the Church's care for the wounded.
Point 3 · The hands of the living God
A severe warning, and the open door of mercy.
live: Look at last month's spending and set aside a fixed share for the poor before anything else.
Choose the hand of the Lord (Hebrews 10:31)
If you have been staying away from confession, go this week; the door is open.
2027-04-20.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you alone are our Master. Deliver us from the love of money and teach us to use the goods of this world in faithfulness and generosity. Bless husbands and wives with faithful love, and surround with your compassion those whose marriages have been broken. Keep us from ever spurning the blood of the covenant, and when we fall, bring us back to the mercy you gave your Church on the evening of your Resurrection. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Blood of the covenant by which we were sanctified is truly given to us; to receive it with faith is to choose the merciful hand of the living God.

quick: We cannot serve God and wealth; money is a servant, not a master.
Jesus restores marriage to God's first plan; the Church upholds it and accompanies the wounded.
Deliberate rejection of Christ's sacrifice leaves no other; but no repented sin is beyond the Church's power to forgive.
2027-04-20.action: Give something today before you spend anything on yourself.
2027-04-20.question: If someone looked at my bank statement and my calendar, whom would they say I serve?

family.explain: Jesus said that nobody can have two bosses at the same time. You cannot serve God and money. Money is useful: we need it for food and school and clothes. But money must never become our boss. God is our only Master, and he wants us to share what we have.
family.intention: We pray for families who are struggling to make ends meet, and for husbands and wives, that they may love each other faithfully.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family share some of our money or things with someone who needs them this week?”

illus: A grocer in Kollam had kept the same shop for thirty years. When his son joined the business, he noticed that the old weighing scale was accurate to the gram and suggested a small adjustment that, he said, every other shop in the market had made. The father took the son to the shrine at the back of the shop, where a small picture of the Sacred Heart hung above the cash box. “This is the one I work for,” he said. “Not the cash box.” The son was annoyed for a few weeks. Years later, when the father died, the queue of customers at the funeral stretched down the road, and many of them said the same thing: “His weight was always true.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are our only Master. Search our hearts tonight and deliver us from every other master. Amen.
share: You cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:13). Where does money compete with God in my life?
God knows your hearts (Luke 16:15). What does God see in my heart that others do not?
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God (Hebrews 10:31). Do I fear God's hands, or trust them?
pm.resp: Lord, you are our only Master.
interc: For the Church, that she may never be ruled by the love of money, and may be rich in mercy.
For those burdened by debt or tempted by dishonest gain.
For husbands and wives, that they may remain faithful to one another until death.
For those whose marriages have broken down, that they may find compassion and accompaniment in the Church.
For all who have stayed away from confession, that they may trust the mercy of the risen Lord.
pm.close: Father, your Son has shown us that we cannot serve two masters. Make us faithful stewards of what you give us, keep our families united in faithful love, and when we sin, bring us back to your merciful hands. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today Jesus says plainly: no slave can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:13). Money is a good servant and a poor master. It asks for the whole heart, and so does God.

St John Chrysostom said that not to share our goods with the poor is to steal from them, for what we hold is also theirs (in substance). The risen Lord asks us to use what passes so as to gain what lasts.

Jesus also restores marriage to the beginning: what God has joined, no one may separate. The Church holds this firmly, and she is also asked to accompany with love those whose marriages have broken, many of whom were hurt against their will.

The Letter to the Hebrews warns: it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. But the fearful thing is to refuse his mercy. On Easter evening Jesus gave the apostles power to forgive sins. Like King David, let us choose to fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercy is great. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: nobody can have two bosses. You cannot serve God and money. Money is useful, but God must always be number one. Can you think of one thing you could share today, a sweet, a toy, a coin, with someone who has less? When we share, we show that God is our boss, not money.

intro: Theme: “You cannot serve God and wealth.”
On this Easter Tuesday: one Master, the covenant of marriage, and the merciful hands of the living God.

sub: Faithful with little, entrusted with much.
Money: a servant, not a master.
q: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil
points.apply: Set aside a fixed share of your income for the poor this month, before other spending.

sub: Accompanying those whose marriages have broken.
q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points.apply: Pray today for a married couple you know who are struggling, and offer them practical help if you can.

points.h: The hands of the living God
sub: The one sacrifice must not be spurned.
The Church keeps the door of Penance open.
“Let us fall into the hand of the Lord.”
q: As I live, says the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live
But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous
points.apply: Go to confession this week if you have been staying away.

concl: Christ alone is our Master; money must serve him and the poor.
God's warnings are the voice of his mercy, calling us back to the one sacrifice and the open door of forgiveness.
2027-04-20.resolve: This week, put God first in your spending, and choose his merciful hand in confession.
